prompt: Many developing countries have built their economies around large-scale international tourism. Do the advantages of this approach outweigh the disadvantages?
essay:
Nowadays, many developing countries are depending on the international tourism for the development of their economy. Some people think this is a good thing but other people disagree. In this essay I will discuss both the advantages and the disadvantages of this situation.

On the one hand, tourism brings many benefits for these countries. Firstly, it creates a lot of the jobs for the local people, for example in the hotels, the restaurants and the transport. Because of this, the unemployment rate become lower and the standard of living is improved. Secondly, the government can earn the foreign currency from the tourists, and they can use this money for building the schools, the hospitals and the roads. Moreover, the tourism also helps to protect the traditional culture, because the tourists want to see the local dances and the handicrafts.

On the other hand, there are some serious disadvantages. Firstly, the tourism can damage the environment very badly. The construction of the big hotels destroy the beaches and the forests, and the tourists produce a lot of garbage. Secondly, the local people sometimes can not afford the houses anymore, because the prices become very high in the tourist areas. In addition, the culture can be affected in the negative way, because the young people copy the behaviour of the foreigners.

In conclusion, the international tourism has the important advantages like the jobs and the money, but it also has the serious disadvantages like the pollution and the high prices. Both of them are very important for the developing countries.
title: Mass tourism in developing economies
